ISUN.GuideBooksP1: This system doesn't come with any Invisible Sun content, not a spell, not a secret, and not a single crystal orb. Invisible Sun is Monte Cook Games' work, and to respect their work and their Fan Use Policy, none of that material is bundled here. Instead, the compendia start out empty so you can fill them directly from the PDFs you own.
ISUN.GuideBooksP2: Place your Invisible Sun books and card decks into a single folder on your computer and point the importer at it. The importer automatically identifies each PDF, extracts the text and card art, and populates your compendia. Everything happens locally in your browser, and your files are never uploaded anywhere.
ISUN.GuideBooksP3: You can safely run the importer more than once as you add new books or decks, and the order of the files doesn't matter. The list below shows what your compendia hold right now.
ISUN.GuideBooksEmptyHint: An empty compendium usually just means it comes from a book or deck you haven't imported yet. The importer shows a full checklist of supported PDFs so you can see what each book fills.
ISUN.GuideWelcomeP1: Welcome to the unofficial Invisible Sun system for Foundry VTT. Invisible Sun works differently from most tabletop roleplaying games, and this system is built from the ground up around how the game is actually played at the table. Your character's stats grow naturally out of their pools, players make all the dice rolls, and the Path of Suns sits on a shared board where everyone can follow every card turn.
ISUN.GuideWelcomeP2: The system is designed to handle the bookkeeping while leaving every real decision in your hands. It tracks your pools, calculates ventures, and keeps a record of active spells, so you don't have to juggle scratch paper. Whenever the rules give you a choice, like whether a Sooth card boosts a spell's level or lowers its cost, or whether to spend bene to shrug off a Wound, the system prompts you with your options and lets you decide.
ISUN.GuideWelcomeGM: The next few pages walk you through what the system offers and how it works in play, covering the character sheet, declaring and resolving rolls, magic and the Path of Suns, Action Mode, and where to find your tools around the screen.
ISUN.GuideWelcomePlayer: The next few pages walk you through your character sheet, how rolls and magic work, Action Mode, and where to find everything on screen. If your character sheet doesn't list any spells, skills, or abilities to pick from yet, don't worry. Your GM just needs to import their Invisible Sun PDFs into the world first.
ISUN.GuideSheetP1: The Overview tab brings together everything you use most during play. At the top sits your character sentence, built from your Foundation, Heart, Order, and Forte. When you assign a Heart, the sheet gives you pool points to distribute directly into your eight pools, including six free points that can go into either Certes or Qualia. Your Certes and Qualia ratings are always the total of their four pools, with Hidden Knowledge tracked alongside them and your skills listed just below.
ISUN.GuideSheetP2: Below your skills, the Overview tab tracks your health, rests, and advancement. Physical and mental Injuries share a single track. When the track fills, the final injury determines whether it becomes a Wound or an Anguish. Armor automatically reduces physical damage before injuries are recorded, and whenever a Wound or Anguish lands, you are prompted with the option to spend bene right then to negate it. Next to your health sits your Advancement panel, tracking your Order degree, Joy, Despair, Acumen, and the Crux formed whenever you pair a Joy with a Despair.
ISUN.GuideSheetP3: The remaining tabs organize the rest of your character's life in the Actuality. Magic holds your spells, incantations, forte abilities, minor magics, secrets, and Secret Soul, along with your Order's special tools, such as the Vance's Mind, the Weaver's Aggregates, the Maker's Bench, or Apostate abilities. Connections, Character Arcs, Inventory & House, and Biography track your bonds, active story beats, orbs and magecoins, ephemera, objects of power, and memories from Shadow. Anything you don't pull from a compendium can be created and edited by hand.
ISUN.GuideRollingP1: In Invisible Sun, only players roll dice. A roll usually begins when the GM clicks the d20 button beside the chat box to declare a challenge, choosing which pool the action draws on, setting the challenge rating, and selecting which characters face it. Players can also start a roll directly from their character sheet by clicking a skill or using a magical practice.
ISUN.GuideRollingP2: To answer a challenge, you build your venture in the roll dialog. Select up to two skills that apply, spend bene from your pool to reduce the difficulty, and spend Sortilege enhancements if you want to add magic dice. As you make your selections, the dialog updates your venture and target number in real time, and tells you immediately if your venture is high enough for an automatic success. A single chat card records the entire exchange.
ISUN.GuideRollingP3: Combat uses this exact same flow. When an opponent acts against a character, the GM marks the challenge as Defensive and the player rolls to defend. If you target a token on the canvas before rolling, the challenge rating is automatically filled in from that target's level along with a reminder of any special defenses they have, though you can always adjust the number before rolling.
ISUN.GuideRollingGM: When declaring a challenge as the GM, selecting a pool determines which pool the player can spend bene from, and automatically brings in any Scourges or Vexes affecting that pool. Scourges penalize every action drawing on that pool, while the Max Vex field lets you decide how many of the character's held vexes to call in against this roll.
ISUN.GuideMagicTitle: Magic and the Path of Suns
ISUN.GuideMagicP1: On the Magic tab, your spells, incantations, forte abilities, and minor magics all live in one filterable Practices list. Clicking Cast pays the Sorcery cost. For a Vance casting a spell held in Mind, it casts for free and asks if you want to spend Sorcery to retain it. When you roll magic dice, rolling a 0 triggers a Magical Flux whose intensity scales with the number of magic dice rolled. If you roll using only the free Experimental Die, it can never produce a success and only checks for flux.
ISUN.GuideMagicP2: Because the rules require players to track their own active spells and depletion checks, the system provides a shared Ongoing Effects board. Active spells and items are grouped by when their depletion is checked, such as at the end of a round, each hour, or each use, letting you roll depletion or end an effect with a single click.
ISUN.GuideMagicP3: The Path of Suns is a shared window for the whole table. As the GM turns Sooth cards onto the suns, the board summarizes every active effect in play. Any venture bonus or penalty a card gives your character is automatically included in your roll dialog, while enhancements or diminishments to a color of magic are shown alongside matching spells on your sheet. This leaves the choice of whether to adjust the spell's level or its Sorcery cost up to the caster.
ISUN.GuideActionP1: Invisible Sun doesn't use initiative rolls. Instead of a fixed turn order, each round in Action Mode works as a checklist. Everyone who can act gets one action in whatever order fits the scene, and the round advances once everyone has taken their turn.
ISUN.GuideActionP2: When you are ready to act, click Take Action on the combat tracker to take the floor, then click Done when you finish, or Wait if you decide not to act yet. Defeated combatants remain listed on the tracker without receiving an action, and hidden tokens are excluded from the tally until they are revealed.
ISUN.GuideActionP3: So you don't have to keep the combat sidebar open during a scene, you can place a Take Action macro on your hotbar from the Invisible Sun scene controls under the cube icon. Clicking that macro once claims the floor for your character, and clicking it again marks your action as Done.
ISUN.GuideActionP4: While Action Mode is running, selecting a token can display range rings for Close, Near, Far, and Very Far scaled to the scene's grid, with new scenes defaulting to 10 feet per square. Player token movement follows the rules automatically. Moving within Close range is free as part of another action, moving past Close up to Near counts as your action for the round and completes your turn, and moving beyond Near in a single round is blocked. Distance is measured across the entire round, so multiple short steps add together.
ISUN.GuideWhereP1: Click the Black Cube icon in the scene controls on the left side of the screen to access the system's tabletop tools, including this Getting Started guide, the Path of Suns board, the Ongoing Effects tracker, the range rings toggle, and the button to add Take Action to your hotbar. GMs also have buttons here to trigger a Magical Flux or start a New Day to rest all chosen characters at once.
ISUN.GuideWhereP2: At the bottom of the Compendium tab on the right sidebar, you'll find a Compendium Search button that searches across every pack at once, along with the PDF importer for the GM. You can also drag any skill or magical practice from your character sheet onto your hotbar at the bottom of the screen to create a quick-use macro.
ISUN.GuideWhereP3: If you run into a bug or spot a rule that doesn't work the way the books describe, please let us know on the GitHub issue tracker. Mentioning the rule and the book and page number makes it easy to track down and fix.

ISUN.MaxVexHint: A ceiling, not a count. What applies is the lesser of this and what the pool holds, and it cannot be declined.
ISUN.IsDefenceHint: An NPC is acting against the character, who rolls to defend.
ISUN.ChallengeGMOnly: Only the GM declares a challenge.
ISUN.ChallengeNoGM: No GM is connected, so the challenge cannot be answered.
ISUN.RollHint: Rolling spends what you have set aside here.
ISUN.ImpossibleReason: No die can reach the target, and there are none spare to try it on.
ISUN.AutoSuccessReason: The venture already meets the challenge.
ISUN.CastNotPrepared: {name} is not in mind. One of the Vance tradition’s own spells has no other way to be cast.
ISUN.CastNotEnoughSorcery: {name} costs {cost} Sorcery and only {pool} is left in the pool.
ISUN.RetainAsk: {name} has been cast. Holding on to it costs {cost} Sorcery, otherwise it leaves your mind.
ISUN.RetainCannotAfford: There is not enough Sorcery left to hold on to it.
ISUN.MigratedSavings: Savings moved into the purse on {count} character(s).
ISUN.MigrationFailed: The Invisible Sun "{id}" migration failed. Your world has not been fully updated. Please check the console and report it before playing on.
ISUN.ImportIntro: To avoid infringing on Monte Cook Game’s copyright, the compendia ship empty. Using this importer, you can fill them from the Invisible Sun PDFs you bought. Your files are read where they are, nothing is uploaded, copied, or stored in Foundry.
ISUN.ImportFound: Found {faces} card faces and {backs} backs, on sheets of {per}.
ISUN.ImportVerified: Checked all {count} cards against the names printed on them.
ISUN.ImportWrongCount: Found {found} card faces, but this deck should have {expected}. Nothing was changed. Is this the right PDF?
ISUN.ImportNothingPages: No cards were read from any of the {pages} pages. Below is what {sampled} sheets sampled across the deck held.
ISUN.ImportNothingPage: Page {page} has {words} pieces of text, {exact} card labels, and {loose} that begin like one.
ISUN.ImportNothingNoText: There is no text layer to read. This looks like a scan or a flattened re-export rather than the self-print PDF.
ISUN.ImportNothingSplit: The labels are on the page, but not as whole pieces of text. This PDF chunks its text differently from the one this reader was written against. That is a fault here, not in your file. Please report it with the line below.
ISUN.ImportNameMismatch: {count} card(s) do not carry the name they were matched to ({first}). Cards are matched to pictures by position, so this would have named them wrongly. Nothing changed.
ISUN.ImportPortraits: Matching portraits… {count} of {total} entries have one.
ISUN.PortraitsProgressHint: Creatures with a picture chosen, of those in the compendium.
ISUN.PortraitsApplyHint: Put the chosen pictures on the actors already in the compendium. The next import does this anyway.
ISUN.PortraitsNoArt: No artwork has been saved yet. Import a book first, as the importer pulls its pictures out while reading it.
ISUN.PortraitsNothingNear: Nothing was printed on this page or either side of it.
ISUN.PortraitsPickOne: Choose a creature on the left.
ISUN.PortraitsBadFile: That file could not be read, {why}
ISUN.ImportStep1: Put the Invisible Sun PDFs you own in one folder. It will sort them out.
ISUN.ImportStep2: Choose that folder below. Your browser will ask you to confirm. It only reads the files.
ISUN.ImportStep3: Press Import. It identifies each file and imports everything it can, and says what it skipped.
ISUN.ImportSizeHint: Only affects decks whose cards are shown as pictures. Larger looks better zoomed in and takes longer to import.
ISUN.EmptyHint: Delete everything in the compendia, so the next import is the only thing in them. An import updates what it recognises and never deletes, so an entry written under a name the books do not use can only go from here.
ISUN.EmptyWarning: This deletes the entries themselves. They are the only copy. Nothing rebuilds them except another import from your PDFs, and anything you have edited by hand will be lost.
ISUN.EmptyArtKept: The card art is kept. It lives outside the system folder, and the next import links it straight back up.
ISUN.EmptyGMOnly: Only a GM can empty the compendia.
ISUN.ImportNoFolder: Choose the folder holding your PDFs first.
ISUN.ImportNoPdfs: That folder has no PDFs in it.
ISUN.ImportFolderScan: Found {pdfs} PDF(s) among {files} file(s). Working out what they are…
ISUN.ImportNotYet: Skipped {file}, recognised as {what}, which this version cannot read yet.
ISUN.ImportUnknown: Skipped {file}, not recognised as an Invisible Sun PDF.
ISUN.ImportNothingToDo: Nothing in that folder can be imported yet.
ISUN.ImportOneDone: Done, {created} new and {updated} existing entries, with {images} images.
ISUN.ImportDeckFirst: That compendium is empty, so there is nothing for this book to fill in. Import the matching deck first. Put both in the folder and the importer will process them in the right order.
ISUN.ImportNothingRead: Nothing was found to import in that book. Is this the right PDF, and the edition this version reads?
ISUN.ImportListingMissing: {count} entries add to things that are not in {pack} yet. Import the matching deck and run this again to give them their prices.
ISUN.ImportPageUnmatched: Page {page} is a card write-up, but names no card in the compendium.
ISUN.ImportValueMismatch: {count} write-up(s) state a value the card disagrees with, starting with {first}. The two halves may be from different printings.
ISUN.ImportBackArt: Cut the deck's card back as the artwork for all {count} entries.
ISUN.ImportFoundCards: Read {count} cards from {sheets} sheets of {columns} columns.
ISUN.ImportClassBacks: Cut {count} card backs, one for each class, {classes}.
ISUN.SourceObjectCardsM: Book M Objects of Power Cards
ISUN.ImportUnplaced: {count} card(s) could not be sorted by the back printed behind them.
ISUN.ActionNobody: Drag tokens in, or add them from the token menu.
ISUN.TargetHardest: Challenge from {name}, level {level}, the hardest of {count} others targeted.
ISUN.MacroNotUsable: {name} is not something that can be used from the bar.
ISUN.MacroNoItem: That is no longer on the character sheet.
ISUN.MacroNotYours: {name} belongs to a character you do not control.
ISUN.MacroNoCreate: You do not have permission to create macros, so it cannot go on the bar.
ISUN.MacroDragHint: Drag onto the hotbar for quick use
ISUN.RangeOverlayHint: Draw the four distance bands around the selected token while Action Mode is running.
ISUN.RangeNoUnits: This scene's grid does not say what its distance is measured in, so the range rings are drawn as feet. Set the units in the scene's grid configuration.
ISUN.TakeActionHint: Take the floor, or say you are done with it.
ISUN.TakeActionNobody: Select the token you are acting with.
ISUN.TakeActionHeld: {name} has the floor. Wait for them to finish.
ISUN.TakeActionDefeated: {name} is out of the fight and gets no action.
ISUN.TakeActionOnBar: Take Action is on your hotbar, slot {slot}.
ISUN.TakeActionBarFull: Your hotbar is full. Move something and try again.
ISUN.TakeActionAdd: Put Take Action on my hotbar
ISUN.TakeActionAlreadyOnBar: Take Action is already on your hotbar, slot {slot}.
ISUN.MoveNotYourGo: It is not {name}'s go. Take the floor first.
ISUN.MoveTooFar: {name} cannot go further than {most} {units} in one round.
ISUN.MoveSpentAction: {name} moved, which was their action. Their go is over.
